title: Mozart: Classical Genius
description: Prodigy to unfinished masterpiece—from child wonder to a mass left incomplete.

questions.question: At what remarkably young age did Mozart compose his first piece of music?
questions.hint: Before he could even write properly, he was creating music
questions.explanation: His father, Leopold, wrote the tiny pieces into sister Nannerl's music book, noting they were "Wolfgangerl's compositions in the first three months after his fifth birthday."

questions.question: Mozart was only five when he began composing—where was he born in 1756?
questions.hint: Known for its salt trade and baroque architecture, now famous for Mozart tours
questions.explanation: In 1756 Salzburg was an independent prince-archbishopric, not yet Austria. In 1781 Mozart quit the archbishop's service—sent off, he told his father, with "a kick in the behind."

questions.question: Salzburg's prodigy later wrote an opera about a legendary seducer—what is it called?
questions.hint: Italian for 'Sir John' - about a legendary seducer who meets a supernatural end
questions.explanation: It premiered in Prague in 1787. In the 'Catalogue Aria,' servant Leporello tallies the Don's conquests: 640 in Italy, 231 in Germany… "but in Spain, already 1,003."

questions.question: After Don Giovanni, his final symphony earned what planetary nickname?
questions.hint: Named after the king of Roman gods - his most majestic symphony
questions.explanation: Mozart never knew the name; it's usually credited to impresario Johann Peter Salomon. He finished it on Aug. 10, 1788, capping three symphonies in roughly two months.

questions.question: Three years after the Jupiter, Mozart died in December 1791 leaving which anonymously commissioned mass for the dead unfinished?
questions.hint: A mass for the dead, left unfinished when the composer himself died
questions.explanation: Forget 'Amadeus': Salieri had nothing to do with it. Mozart's pen stopped eight bars into the Lacrimosa; his widow had pupil Süssmayr finish it so she could collect the fee.

deeperMode.description: Mozart's eccentric personality and the mysteries surrounding his death

questions.question: Mozart had a peculiar sense of humor. What bodily function did he frequently reference in letters and even compose music about?
questions.hint: He wrote several pieces with scatological titles and jokes about this natural bodily function

questions.question: What mysterious figure commissioned Mozart's final Requiem, leading to legends about death itself ordering the piece?
questions.hint: A count who wanted to pass off the work as his own composition for his wife's memorial
